title: Netflow Python library – A free software tool for the generation and analysis of pore or flow networks
author: Meyer
materials: Class of a throat connecting two pores.
simplenet.connect_pores(pore1=source, pore2=pore, r=0.05) # connect to source

steps.title: Load and plot demo network
steps.instruction: Import matplotlib and the netflow package, load the demo network from the HDF5 file 'network.h5' using netflow.load_network_from, and plot it with netflow.plot_network.

steps.title: Generate simple periodic network
steps.instruction: Create a periodic cubical network with 1e2 uniformly distributed pores, target size [2,1.5,0.5], pore radius 0.01, throat radius 0.001, coordination number 4, maximum edge length 0.45, and random seed 1; then plot it.

substeps.instruction: simplenet = netgen.generate_simple_net(n_pores=1e2, targetsize=[2,1.5,0.5], r_pore=0.01, r_throat=0.001, coordinatnumb=4, Lmax=0.45, sd=1)

steps.title: Generate dendrogram network from demo
steps.instruction: Generate a periodic network that preserves pore clusters from the previously loaded demo network using generate_dendrogram with target size [1,1,1], cutoff equal to half the base network length in the first dimension, seed 1, and mute=True; then plot it.

steps.title: Open periodic throats in directions 1 and 2
steps.instruction: Open periodic throat connections crossing the domain faces in the c‑directions 1 and 2 for the simple network, using a dictionary to avoid duplicate pore copies, and plot the result.

substeps.instruction: inouts = {}  # dictionary to store copied pores

steps.title: Cut network with planar plane
steps.instruction: Apply a cutting plane normal to the c‑axis (c=1) at position x=0.5 to the simple network, creating pores of radius 0 at intersection points, and plot the cut network.

steps.title: Erase network portion left of cut
steps.instruction: Remove all pores (and their throats) located to the left of x=0.5 along c=1, labeling the removed side as 'inlet', then plot the remaining network.

steps.title: Add single inlet pore and connect to face pores
steps.instruction: Create a new pore at position [0,0.75,0.25] with radius 0 and label 'in1', add it to the simple network, then connect it to every pore whose label is 'inlet' (clearing their label) using throat radius 0.05, and plot the updated network.

steps.title: Solve flow for non‑periodic network
steps.instruction: Define the inlet pore set containing the source pore and the outlet pore set containing all pores labelled 'out1'; solve the steady‑state flow with inlet pressure 1e4 Pa, outlet pressure 0 Pa, and viscosity 1e-3 kg/(m·s); then plot pressure bubbles (size proportional to pressure/1e4 × 400), outlet pores (green), and flux throats (red) with linewidth max(0.5, |flux| × 2e6).

substeps.instruction: outpores = {pore for pore in simplenet.pores if pore.label == 'out1'}
(press, flux) = netflow.solve_flow_inout(simplenet, pin=1e4, pout=0, inpores=inpores, outpores=outpores, mu=1e-3)
pnts = [pore.pos for pore in press]; pnts = list(map(list, zip(*pnts)))
size = [p/1e4 * 400 for pore, p in press.items()]
pnts = [pore.pos for pore in outpores]; pnts = list(map(list, zip(*pnts)))

steps.title: Check flux balance and plot results
steps.instruction: Compute the flux balance for all pores, print the total inflow through the source pore, remove the inlet and outlet pores from the balance dictionary, then plot outgoing, incoming, and net flux versus pore index with appropriate labels.

substeps.instruction: print('the total inflow into the network is %e' % Qb[source][2])
Qb = {pore: Qb[pore] for pore in Qb if (pore not in inpores) and (pore not in outpores)}
Qp = [Qb[k][0] for k in Qb]; Qm = [Qb[k][1] for k in Qb]; Qs = [Qb[k][2] for k in Qb]
plt.plot(x, Qp, x, Qm, x, Qs)

steps.title: Solve flow for periodic network
steps.instruction: Set viscosity mu=1e-3 kg/(m·s), pressure drop per length P2L=1e2 Pa/m, and direction c=3; solve the periodic flow on the dendrogram network; adjust each pore pressure by subtracting the mean pressure component P2L*(pore.pos[c‑1]‑dendronet.lb[c‑1]); then plot pressure bubbles colored by normalized pressure using the plasma colormap and plot non‑periodic throats (label == '') as thin black lines.

substeps.instruction: pnts = [pore.pos for pore in press]; pnts = list(map(list, zip(*pnts)))

steps.title: Save and load flow solutions
steps.instruction: Use netflow.save_flow_to to write pressure and flux data to an HDF5 file and netflow.load_flow_from to read them back.
